items.title: Silksong is getting a free expansion in 2 weeks
items.summary:
In a "Cherry Time!" presentation , Hollow Knight developer Team Cherry has just revealed a first look at its much-anticipated first content update to Hollow Knight: Silksong. The nautical-themed Sea of Sorrow will come as a free update on December 11.

Team Cherry said that Sea of Sorrow will contain multiple new areas, power-ups, and bosses, while I clocked at least three new friendly NPCs in the trailer: A townsperson, a new shopkeeper, and a ferryman. Area-wise, I made out three distinct tilesets in the trailer: A rain-blasted fishing town on the water, a harrowing climb with an electrical storm element, and a green space reminiscent of the early game Bell Bottom.

At least the first of these areas appears to be built on cut content for Silksong: "Pharloom Bay" is well-documented on the Hollow Knight wiki , and would have been located on the east side of the map, near the thematically-similar Greymoor. Some elements in the trailer correspond to ones documented by the wiki, like an underwater submersible vehicle, or a scientific lab in the electrical storm area.

Which all sounds rad to me, particularly the submersible. Among the all-timer videogame level concepts, "underwater techbase" is one of my very favorites, and Team Cherry seem to be approaching these concepts with a Lovecrafty, Innsmouth flair that reminds me of the Fishing Village zone from Bloodborne.

Silksong is already a massive game, and I'm curious as to how Sea of Sorrow will fit both the map, and the game's overall flow from act to act. We'll find out for sure when the free expansion releases on…
items.t: Silksong is getting a free expansion in 2 weeks

items.title: I Tried to Get Six Stars in GTA 6 With Just One Bullet and Broke the Game

If reaching a six-star wanted level in Grand Theft Auto 6 is your goal, there are many different methods available to you. Raiding the military base for a tank is one way. Committing a horrifying beach massacre is another. But can you get there by firing just a single bullet? We at IGN had a theory that this was absolutely possible, and so spent hours in a fast food joint to find out.

When we say “by firing a single bullet,” we mean that technically speaking. Our theory is that your chosen character only needs to pull the trigger once. That’s because, when roaming around GTA 6’s open world and causing whatever brand of chaos you’ve chosen to, your partner will automatically take up the fight against aggressors, and is both invulnerable and stocked with unlimited ammunition. That means if you decide to walk into a heavily populated area as a couple and fire just one bullet into the crowd, your better half can commit the lion's share of the atrocities themselves, provided you just stay alive.

We tested this out for ourselves, leading Jason and Lucia to the Taco Bomb in Gellhorn as our chosen arena of violence. Taking control of Jason, one bullet was fired into a poor staff member taking a break outside. Bits of brain now covered the forecourt, which somehow still looked like a more appetising alternative to whatever the questionable-looking beef was they were offering inside. items.title: Hollow Knight: Silksong - Sea of Sorrow Launch Trailer Finally Confirms Release Date, Teases Fishing
items.summary:
Team Cherry has just wrapped up its Cherry Time! showcase, giving us some long-awaited news on the future of Hollow Knight: Silksong.

The big takeaway here is that Hollow Knight: Silksong's first big expansion, Sea of Sorrow, finally has a release date of December 11. Sea of Sorrow will be available to all Silksong players for free. All you need is a copy of the base game, and you can start playing Sea of Sorrow when it goes live on December 11.

This also means Team Cherry has stuck to its promise to get Sea of Sorrow out by the end of the year. Some had feared that today's announcement would be a delay — or an announcement that the DLC was being expanded into a full game, which is famously how Silksong's development began. 

In the showcase, we got a new look at Sea of Sorrow's gameplay. This gives us a good preview of what's in store for us, as we see new areas, enemies, and boss fights. Of course, it all looks as challenging as ever, as you'd expect for Silksong's post-launch DLC. And is that a fishing mini-game teased at the end?

We weren't told anything else about the future of Silksong or the Hollow Knight series at large. There was no mention of this being Silksong's only expansion, so it's very possible that Team Cherry plans to support the game beyond Sea of Sorrow. 

For now, here's the official blurb on Sea of Sorrow:

In Sea of Sorrow, players will voyage above and beneath Pharloom’s forgotten ocean, across islands, through forts and into deep caverns beneath the waves. We’ve spent the whole year stuffing this adventure full with all the things you’d expect…

items.title: On Top of Everything Else, GTA 6 Is a Solid Stealth Sandbox

Grand Theft Auto is a boisterous, brash series full of loud characters and louder explosions. GTA 6 continues that tradition for many of its main story beats, chaining showy set-pieces into lethal car chases, but in my 35 hours roaming Leonda I've found plenty of chances to engage with its surprisingly robust stealth system. In some cases, it even feels like Rockstar specifically designed areas with sneaking and silencers in mind. 

Illegal operations are lucrative robbery opportunities dotted around the map that hide cash, jewellery, drugs, and unique items – cars, weapons, watches – guarded by armies of enemies. I struggled with them early on: shooting my way to the valuables attracted GTA 6's menacing police, curtailing my heists before I could grab all the loot and forcing me to flee across entire counties while a chopper buzzed overhead. 

Now, I treat these scenarios like stealth vignettes, my goal to remain hidden for as long as possible. items.title: Microsoft announces it's deprecating the Telnet client in Windows, giving me a sudden flashback to when I used to use Telnet
items.summary:
In its latest update on deprecated features in Windows , Microsoft casually mentioned that "Telnet Client is deprecated and will be removed from Windows in a future release."

This may not mean much to you if you didn't do a lot of computer networking in the 1990s or earlier, but the text-based protocol for remotely opening command-line interfaces was a workhorse we used for a bunch of things. It's how antique university lab computers that didn't even have Netscape Navigator installed connected to the internet, how I played text-based online games like the Discworld MUD back in the day, and how we used to connect to our routers.

By default, Telnet didn't encrypt all the data it was swapping back and forth between computers, which is why it's since been replaced by tools like SSH and PowerShell. So it's not a surprise that it's being deprecated, and honestly I'm impressed that it outlived both WordPad and Cortana . 

A Windows feature being deprecated means that it won't be in active development and is a candidate for removal in a future update, so Telnet isn't being 86ed immediately. If you're still using it to test network connections because that's what you're used to then carry on as you were, but get ready to grumble and switch over to PowerShell when Microsoft finally does pull the plug.
items.t: Microsoft announces it's deprecating the Telnet client in Windows, giving me a sudden flashback to when I used to use Telnet

Though Vermintide 2's had a Steam Workshop since 2018, it's mostly used for quality-of-life stuff like UI tweaks. That's set to change now that Fatshark has announced a public release of its internal developer tools, which they say "will allow modders to work their magic on both editing and creating anything from custom levels, models, textures, particles, animations, and more!"

Right now, only a select number of sanctioned mods can be used in Vermintide 2's "official realm" which is the one with loot and leveling that carries over, while unsanctioned mods can only be accessed in a "modded realm" where there are no progression systems. Obviously that's off-putting to a lot of players, so Fatshark has announced a change.

"We have an update releasing in early December which will see the Modded Realm have its own, local, offline progression. That means that playing in the Modded Realm will still result in you gaining loot and experience, but said progression will not reflect on the Official Realm. This should make playing on the Modded Realm feel much better and not be discouraging for those that want to try out all of the unsanctioned mods, both the ones that already exist and the ones to come thanks to the Mod Tools!"

I'm not sure how many players will be happy to start over from level one just to get access to a wider variety of mods, but I hope it encourages some folks to check them out. 25% of Rockstar employees voted in favor of the recognition agreement, the union said, while 75% voted against it. 1,544 employees took part in the vote, representing a turnout of just over 93%.

Rockstar workers actually founded a union earlier this year—the Rockstar Game Workers Union, a subsidiary of the Independent Workers Union of Great Britain—and it will continue to operate as it has. The IWGB said the outcome will not prevent Rockstar workers from organizing or exercising union rights, but the company will not be required to regularly meet with union representatives for collective bargaining or other relevant matters. 

Despite the vote, the union said it will continue with organizing efforts at Rockstar.

"For anyone at Rockstar who believes in a fairer workplace, a fairer sector and a fairer society—this isn’t a sign to retreat, it’s a sign to double down on what we stand for. items.title: Should you participate in GTA 6's Safe Word mission?
items.summary:
Deciding whether to participate or not in GTA 6 's Safe Word mission is tricky. On the one hand, you don't want to blow your cover, on the other, the setup is incredibly funny. Jason and Lucia head to a mansion to steal a safe, masquerading as pool cleaners, but once Jay heads inside, it's clear that he's actually playing a poolboy in an erotic flick.

While applying lotion to the female performers, Lucia will get increasingly agitated in his earpiece, and then you'll finally have to choose whether to actually participate in the scene or not:

Participate : This will negatively impact your romance with Lucia and since the outcome is the same (Lucia immediately interrupts the scene by setting off a car alarm), Jason doesn't actually do anything. As Rockstar has previously said, you can't cheat on Lucia . After you leave the scene, Lu will be a little angry, but it won't hang over things. Don't Participate : This will positively impact your romance and as above, the car alarm will immediately go off afterwards, ending the scene anyway. Jason will say he needs to go to the bathroom and make his way inside the mansion, continuing the mission to find and steal the safe. So, on the whole, choosing not to participate is better if you care about your romance level and how it might impact things later. If not, say what you will.

The first game's a schlocky high school romance generally considered a chore to get through before the good stuff, when the protagonist of that story finds himself out of his depth as a mecha pilot fighting aliens in an apocalyptic warzone. It becomes a dense, twisty, and increasingly serious saga that just happens to star a dropkick hero right out of a harem anime.

Muv-Luv's popular enough to have a bunch of spin-offs, the latest being a gacha game called Muv-Luv Girls Garden in which you collect girls to pilot mecha in automated battles, and of course said girls are romanceable. This caused a problem, as players discovered when they made it to some of the adult scenes only to find dialogue in which characters repeated at each other, "I can't provide a translation for explicit sexual content."

items.title: Inside Retro Reset, the "really inspirational" father and son project teaching kids about classic games hardware from aboard a converted bus
items.summary: At first the kids jostle to get to the games that they know. "Welcome to the Retro Reset Bus," says Luke Stoner as the students push to get to the screen that’s caught their eye. Sonic on the Sega Mega Drive is the first they see, and the quickest student to get on board the bus looks triumphant as he nabs the stool in front of the console. Jason, Luke’s dad, asks him what he thinks about the graphics – slightly grainy and slightly pixelated – but he’s not at all bothered and soon engrossed. After a few minutes, though, his eyes keep moving to the back of the bus where "Jackson is a wally" is now emblazoned across a flickering screen in seven different colours. Jackson then gives out a chuffed yell when his code finally works after a couple of restarts. His retort to his mate appears on the 1981 BBC Micro Model B‘s screen as the other students crane to have a look. This is, incidentally, the machine that turned a national broadcaster into a computer retailer (with help from Acorn), says Jason.
items.t: Inside Retro Reset, the "really inspirational" father and son project teaching kids about classic games hardware from aboard a converted bus
